unresolvedReferences.description: 贈柳宜城 / 'Liu of Yicheng' is recorded as a title of Liu Hun because he is the Liu of this biography. The chapter never says Liu Hun was connected with Yicheng, so the link is uncertain.
舅源休明逆伏誅 is read as maternal uncle Yuan Xiu openly rebelling and being executed. The printed English treats Yuan Xiuming as the name. A repair is proposed; the surface keeps the printed English.
元琇 is romanized Yuan Xiu, the same English form as 源休, Cui Zao's maternal uncle in the preceding chunk. They are different people. The surface keeps the printed English.
元平兒 / 'Li Yuanping's boy' is Li Xilie's taunt that the beardless captive looked like a child. It is not a son, and no child is created.
其上心 is read as Daizong, the emperor of Liang Zhen's Guangde memorial earlier in this chapter, not Dezong, who is the emperor of the Jianzhong narrative.
太公 is treated as legendary antiquity because this unit only calls him an ancient great sage and gives no convertible date. He is traditionally the early-Zhou Taigong.
